_comment: check-cg selftest: three repeater instantiations in rtl/top/rpt-units.json's form (tools/gen-top.py). One stage of one 64-bit slot, with a 16-bit lead slice and without: the lead's first-stage flops, written every cycle, take the instantiation past its own allowance; without them it passes. Two stages of a 16-bit slot: its nine control flops (valid, wake, credit and stall at each stage, and the flopped reset) are past a 41-flop module's allowance, and pass it because they count against the wrapper's budget instead (Daniel, 2026-10-19). The first three are at BOUNDARY 0, the link's stages alone. Two more carry the 16-bit lead at BOUNDARY 1 (DA tab rev 108, AR rev 289): with no link stage, the boundary flop is the first stage, and its ungated lead slice, bnd_lead_q, counts against the wrapper's budget (the receiving or sending block's), so the instantiation passes; at a destination end behind one link stage, the boundary is the last, gated stage, the first is a link stage, and its lead_q is still the repeater's own and past its allowance.
